speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Prime Minister how will the Government build a Smart Nation that (i) is inclusive and people-centric rather than technology-centric in the implementation of e-services and cashless transactions respectively and (ii) ensures that Government services can still be easily accessed by elderly Singaporeans of all backgrounds.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked	the Prime Minister (a) if he can provide an update on the Smart Nation programme; (b) whether there are plans to bring pervasive technologies into the daily lives of Singaporeans; and (c) how does the Government intend to achieve its Smart Nation vision moving forward.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Each has a timeline for delivery that includes intermediate milestones.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: While critical to the Smart Nation's success, these and future SNPs are not outcomes in and of themselves.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do not chase technology for technology's sake.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Instead, we must be people-centric, as Dr Tan Wu Meng has said.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are three levels of outcomes that we strive for under Smart Nation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: First, at the individual level, Smart Nation must bring about practical convenience and a higher quality of life.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Next, at the enterprise level, Smart Nation must boost efficiency, reduce costs and stimulate business.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the banking industry are working to extend PayNow to merchants and companies.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The SGQR will provide merchants with an infrastructure-light and cheaper alternative to accept different types of e-payments, including PayNow.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There will be new ways of doing things, new forms of businesses and new jobs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Businesses will be transformed through end-to-end digitalisation of their processes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Digital platforms will allow our enterprises to tap new markets.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Government will keep standards and platforms open so that as many enterprises as possible can take advantage of the opportunities.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have been and will continue to actively work together with the private sector.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To achieve these outcomes, Smart Nation needs to be a whole-of-nation endeavour.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This means benefiting and involving all segments of the population, including the elderly.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We must strive to provide digital options that are user-friendly for all.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For example, the Post Office Savings Bank (POSB) is working with some primary schools to explore child-friendly e-payment options, from wearables to biometric payment.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We should similarly develop solutions to help the elderly embrace e-payments and other digital opportunities.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We must be a nation of smart users and exploiters of technology.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We should neither blindly adopt technology nor shut it out and refuse to change.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This requires us to be prepared to try new things and pick up new skills.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Reskilling is not easy but it is necessary, which is why we have put in place SkillsFuture and programmes, such as the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA's) TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) to help all Singaporeans be digitally ready.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We must enable digital access and we must also facilitate digital readiness to help everyone have the skills and literacy to use digital technology in a safe, responsible and confident way, and give everyone the ability and opportunity to participate meaningfully in the digital society.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Basic digital skills are something we need to equip everyone with.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In the 1980s, when we saw a wave of computerisation across offices in Singapore, moving from typewriters to word processing, the Public Service took the lead through the National Computerisation Plan to implement widespread training of basic computer skills.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are now facing another major need for such a movement, and we will have to ensure everyone is equipped with a set of basic digital skills, be it for work or in our daily lives.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) has set up a Digital Readiness Workgroup with representatives from the public and private sectors who have expertise and experience in applying technology to make lives better.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: An important part of being digitally ready is to understand the risks involved and to be proactive in risk mitigation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Financial institutions in Singapore have been taking measures to detect and deter cyber threats and strengthen the security of their digital platforms.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MAS has set standards and expectations for financial institutions on the management of technology risks.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But, as with other forms of payment, such as cash or cheque, the individual also has to exercise the responsibility to protect himself.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In e-payments, there are simple steps that each of us can take to protect against fraudulent transactions or identity theft.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MAS has been working closely with the banking industry and law enforcement agencies to raise consumer awareness of these measures.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Singapore Police Force (SPF) and the National Crime Prevention Council (NCPC) have also conducted several anti-scam public education initiatives over the years as well, and launched the Anti-Scam Helpline.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We need to step up these efforts as we advance along the Smart Nation journey.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is about building a strong society and economy for all, where businesses thrive, opportunities abound and we look forward with confidence to the future.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Change is uncomfortable, but, if not for some of the bold, uncomfortable changes our founding leaders had the vision to make, Singapore will not be where we are today.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Not only have we survived, but we have thrived.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The nation-building narrative of the next generation will be about digital infrastructure as much as it is about physical infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Before my questions, I just want to declare my interest.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I do work in a financial institution that offers payment services.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether the Government would take a more regulatory stance, such as the payment players to collaborate with one another, or the Government may take a more developmental incentivising approach here.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Our role is really to ensure that there are common platforms and standards of interoperability, and then, in parallel, to make sure that all the regulations, oversight, compliance and enforcement around our monetary system and our financial system continue to be robust and relevant to both the technologies and the opportunities that the waves of digitalisation will make possible.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have worked with a number of players to introduce PayNow.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are working to increase adoption of QR codes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will continue to take a balance between a regulatory stance as well as developmental.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But, really, we have to ensure that whoever is making these proposals, the standards are maintained.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have several proposals to do so and we will study all the proposals that are put before us.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I understand that the move towards Smart Nation is a future-oriented one and it is to provide the options, the foundation for those who are ready to embrace it.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But again, back to the elderly, and it may not just include those who are single, lonely elderly who have no family members to support them, and, if they do not have banking accounts, just wondering whether the Government will also focus on how we can help them to have a better understanding and more trust in the system because that is one of the obstacles.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The other one is that to go cashless, one of the intermediaries is to have cards.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Some of them may not know how to use cards.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: They may have lost it, they may have forgotten the passwords.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Therefore, will we consider using biometric more, so that wherever they go, it becomes easier for them and it is also more robust in terms of identification and they can engage in these services more seamlessly?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The second part of this is a slight deviation but also relevant.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As we endeavour towards Smart Nation, will the Government continue to ensure that the elderly or those who prefer face-to-face interaction will not be unwittingly shut out of the whole communication and feedback process because there is a strong reliance on the e-mode, the digital mode?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But there are those who would prefer very much to rely on the face-to-face mode for communications, for example, going to a Ministry to give feedback or make enquiries.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, I would like to get the Senior Minister of State's indication on these.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Our general approach going forward is, rather than look at a singular form factor, whether it is a fob or a card, our general approach has been to try to look at software solutions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: One of the reasons for this is that it can then be incorporated into a number of form factors.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For example, if you had a phone which accepted biometric authentication, and you use that to access your software platform, that would be a different approach from someone who used a personal identification number (PIN) to access the same software.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, using software as a middle layer to allow engagements through a variety of form factors, is certainly part of the design principles of how we would do to increase adoption and utilisation of Smart Nation initiatives.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If I could use an example to answer both the first and third questions from Ms Tin, the first question was about how we could help the elderly have trust in the system and the third question was about maintaining a face-to-face interaction.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: One is the Housing and Development Board (HDB) and the other is our CitizenConnect Centres.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: HDB has significantly digitalised much of its customer-facing processes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It has used backend software improvements, it has used user interfaces.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But there is still a lot of staff in the office, in the branches, at the counters, not to remove the need for human interaction but to change the nature of that human interaction, so that when customers step in, the staff are there with tablets, with the computers, guiding potential home owners through the process and helping them to navigate the process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, rather than having staff deal with laborious data entry or merely deal with the process management, the HDB staff have been reskilled towards customer relations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Another example is our CitizenConnect Centres where individuals who do not have access to a computer or a phone, or do not have the confidence to deal with Government services online, can go to these CitizenConnect Centres.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Most of them are located within Community Centres.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Why have we got the solution this way?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Because it means that we give people access to e-services if they do not have a computer, a phone or the confidence, but also, there is an opportunity for the staff to interact with these citizens and explain to them the process, help them onboard, perhaps teach them so that they may be able to do it next time, or if they bring along a family member, staff can teach them, and to help them develop trust in the system.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we have used that as solution, not just to provide people access and participation, but also to try to help to develop trust in the e-services and public services that are made available through the online centres.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have two supplementary questions which I would like to set in context as well.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: By illustration, I mention an anecdote where my resident showed me a letter from an agency, written in English, saying that e-services would replace manual forms and asking the residents to get ready with their SingPass and two-factor authentication.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But some of these residents were elderly, not quite familiar, and sadly, became quite concerned.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The reason for this is, again, to make it easy enough that people transition without the solution being imposed on them.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Because, if I may say, as part of a Smart Nation, we need smart design, inclusive design, with Singaporeans, for Singaporeans, for Singapore.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On the first question, which is essentially about digital inclusion, certainly, English literacy, I suspect, is as big a problem, if not a greater problem than just age, for adoption.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The simple answer would be to recommend for our resident to approach the Community Centre and CitizenConnect Centre where people can help him or her access that service, conduct their online business if necessary or, if possible, teach them how to do so.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But it is not going to be enough to just assume it would improve over time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are segments of the population that we would have to reach out to especially, and we would have to think about what are the channels within the community that we can leverage to reach out to them.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we welcome suggestions on how we can find people who are having difficulty engaging with Government services online and reach out to them better.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The second question Dr Tan asked was about the user interface.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are also increasing the use of talent in the user interface phase, so that when we do the engineering, we have people with user interface, user experience talent, looking at the design process right from the start.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is an informed part of how we make sure that people can participate.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For example, the size of the text, the contrast ratio, providing captions, providing spoken language options as well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we have a variety of standards and we are taking a whole-of-Government approach to this.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Would the Senior Minister of State agree that with the rollout of Smart Nation, especially e-payment systems which will be pervasive, and especially since it will involve the elderly, the security risks and reliability of the transactions and the e-payment systems would be quite different from what he is talking about, that is, MAS' guidelines on financial institutions.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Are we ready to face the challenge of security risks, in terms of e-payment, and what measures are we looking at?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In terms of the Smart Nation initiative moving forward, the question is what are we comparing these e-payments to?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If we care comparing them to cash, then e-payments are certainly more secure.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Because you can track, you can trace, you can authenticate identity and provenance and so on and so forth.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But if we are comparing them to, for example, credit cards, EZ-Link, Network for Electronic Transfers (NETs) − these are all non-cash e-payment solutions that we have had for some time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have some experience in operating and regulating these systems and monitoring these systems, and in detecting and deterring threats and theft associated with these systems.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: When we engage with citizens and, especially with the elderly, we should highlight that, actually, we have had e-payment solutions in Singapore for a long time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I have just highlighted some of them − NETS, EZ-Link, credit cards.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have a lot of e-payment transactions that are occurring today.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We must increase the level of trust that we have in the security of our systems.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is a very important question and we have quite a lot of work going on in exactly that realm.
